# Operations checklist

Work through this before running `product-definition change validate`. Each entry names the
diagnostic that fires when the check is skipped.

## Deciding add vs modify vs remove

- `add` only for IDs absent from the baseline. Adding an ID that already exists is PRODUCT020 —
  if the artifact exists and you want it different, the operation is `modify`.
- `modify` only for IDs present in the baseline, and the proposed artifact keeps the same ID.
  Modifying a nonexistent ID is PRODUCT021 — if it does not exist yet, the operation is `add`.
- `remove` only for IDs present in the baseline. Removing a nonexistent ID is PRODUCT022.
- Renaming is not an operation: model it as `remove` old ID + `add` new ID, and repair every
  reference to the old ID in proposed artifacts, or removal leaves dangling references.

## Overlay coherence

- No two artifacts in the overlay may share an ID; an `add` colliding with another active
  change's addition, or duplicated proposed files, is PRODUCT023.
- For every `remove`, run `product-definition impact <ID> --direction incoming` and give each
  active referrer a proposed future state that drops the reference, or the removal dangles
  (PRODUCT024).
- Check other active changes' `modify`/`remove` lists; any overlap with yours is PRODUCT025
  until one change is rebased or withdrawn.

## proposed/ completeness and base-revision

- Every ID in `add`/`modify` has exactly one complete file under `proposed/`, and every file
  under `proposed/` is listed in operations — either mismatch is PRODUCT026. `remove` entries
  get no tombstone file.
- Proposed files are full future-state artifacts, never diffs or edit instructions, and mirror
  the `docs/product/model` layout with filenames matching lowercase IDs (PRODUCT101 warns).
- `base-revision` is the exact `git rev-parse HEAD` at creation; a stale value blocks promotion
  later (PRODUCT027), so refresh it consciously if the baseline moves before approval.
